Financial strength and the price paid
109 investments. 100 company financial reviews. Two new decision factors.

The summary tables now include Financial Strength (FS, 0-100), a short growth-funding interpretation, and
Price-Fundamentals Balance. Every company has a C001-C100 dossier covering its income statement, balance
sheet, cash flow, multi-year history and material financial caveats. Renewable summaries now use the same 12
columns as the other investment summaries.

 New parameter                   What it answers                                What it does not establish
 Financial Strength              Can profits, cash, liquidity and capital       A stock-return forecast, credit rating or guarantee of
                                 support growth without excessive financial     financial safety.
                                 strain?
 Price-Fundamentals Balance      Do reported earnings and cash broadly          A fair-value target, a full DCF or a personalized buy/sell
                                 support the price, or does it need demanding   instruction.
                                 future assumptions?

Financial funding profile. 36 strong, 26 sound, 18 mixed, 18 weak, 2 fragile. These are rubric results across
different business models, not percentiles or credit-risk probabilities.

Price support at the reviewed ratios. 7 supported, 28 conditional, 35 demanding, 1 funding-sensitive, 29 not
established. “Supported” means passing a limited current earnings/cash screen; it does not remove country,
governance, competition or valuation-model risk.

How to use this update. Read the two new columns together, then open the matching C-number dossier. High
FS plus a demanding price can be a strong business with a substantial valuation hurdle. A low multiple with weak
cash funding can be a value trap. The original qualitative success-factor grades, growth flags and three-year
scenario outputs remain separate.

Reading order. F2-F5 explain methods, F6-F7 locate all 100 companies, then the updated E/S/core research
sections provide all 109 investment summaries. The C001-C100 financial dossiers follow those sections,
beginning at F8. PDF bookmarks link each company.

Scope and cutoff. Standardized statements and valuation ratios were reviewed October 28, 2026; each dossier labels the actual
reporting period. Earlier market caps, forward multiples, entry quotes and scenarios retain their original October 27/28 observation
times. This update does not silently reprice those forecasts. Results scheduled after the research cutoff are excluded.

What the financial review covers
Income and growth. Up to three completed fiscal years plus the latest available TTM or annual view: revenue,
operating profit, net income, EPS, diluted shares and margins. The reported revenue CAGR spans the two
intervals between three annual observations; it is historical, not a forward forecast.

Balance sheet. Cash/short investments, total debt, net cash or debt, current liquidity, equity and
tangible/intangible exposure. Debt generally includes leases in the comparison data. It is not total liabilities.
Customer deposits, deferred revenue, pension, project and minority claims need separate interpretation.

Cash and allocation. Operating cash, capital investment, free cash, stock compensation, equity financing,
repurchases and dividends. Three-year positive-profit/FCF counts test persistence. Cash raised by issuing shares
or debt is not operating cash generation.

Material issuer context. Issuer releases, annual/interim reports and selected filing notes support
company-specific interpretation. These include unusual gains/tax items, acquisitions, advance payments, capital
raises and regulatory capital. The review does not independently audit every standardized line, covenant,
maturity, contractual commitment or legal contingency.

Data provenance. The numerical comparison tables use Stock Analysis standardized statements/ratios, which
attribute data to S&P; Global Market Intelligence or Fiscal.ai. Company financial reports are linked separately. The
connected Massive plan did not provide the statement dataset; these figures are not described as Massive data.
Some issuer documents are hosted by filing mirrors, identified by their linked host.

Missing and asynchronous data. N/D means not displayed or not available; a dash is not assumed zero. N/M
means a ratio is not economically meaningful. Latest income, balance and cash dates can differ; matched annual
periods are used for cash scoring where needed. Short public histories earn fewer persistence points. A latest
annual column can repeat the first fiscal-year column.

Currency and share bases. All financial tables use the issuer statement currency in millions, except EPS/ratios
and shares in millions. Foreign home-market statements are not USD ADR statements. Ratios are taken directly
from the cited vendor page, avoiding currency conversion and ADR-share arithmetic. A vendor ratio can still use a
different earnings/share denominator or update time.

Financial Strength: the operating rubric
FS measures current financial funding strength. It is a transparent analyst screen, not an empirically trained
model of successful stocks. Weights total 100. A 100 means every displayed criterion earned full points; it does
not mean risk-free. Differences below roughly 5-10 points are not decision-grade precision.

Pillar / maximum                 Point rules before disclosed company adjustments

Profitability and quality / 25   Operating margin: ≥25%=15; ≥15%=12; ≥5%=9; >0=5. Add 2 per positive-net-income annual year
                                 (max 6), plus 4 if current operating and net profit are positive. Quality caps address material
                                 nonoperating/tax effects.

Cash generation / 25             FCF margin: ≥15%=15; ≥5%=12; >0=8. Add 2 per positive-FCF annual year (max 6). OCF/net income
                                 (positive NI): ≥1.0=4; ≥0.8=3; ≥0.5=1. Matched annual flows replace mismatched latest periods.
                                 Specified quality caps apply.

Liquidity / 20                   Current ratio: ≥2=10; ≥1.3=8; ≥1=5; ≥0.75=2. Cash/current liabilities: ≥1=10; ≥0.5=8; ≥0.2=5;
                                 ≥0.1=2. For a loss-making cash burner instead: static cash/annual FCF burn runway ≥36 months=20,
                                 ≥24=16, ≥12=10, ≥6=5.

Leverage and service / 20        Net cash: 15 debt points. Otherwise net debt/positive EBITDA: ≤1=12; ≤2.5=9; ≤4=5. Operating
                                 profit/interest: ≥10=5; ≥5=4; ≥2=2; ≥1=1. Missing interest with net cash receives a disclosed 4/5
                                 fallback. Captive-finance exceptions are separate.

Share allocation / 10            Annual diluted-share two-year CAGR: ≤0=10; ≤2%=8; ≤5%=6; ≤10%=3; >10%=0. Insufficient
                                 comparable history=3. Latest SBC/revenue >15% caps this at 2; >10% caps it at 5. Buybacks are not
                                 automatically good if they weaken capital.


Bands: 80-100 Strong; 60-79 Sound; 40-59 Mixed; 20-39 Weak; 0-19 Fragile. These describe this funding rubric.
They are not investment grades. Regulated utilities, project developers and clinical research can deliberately
consume cash; a low self-funding score does not by itself establish insolvency.

Growth support: high FS with positive residual cash can fund reinvestment internally; lower FS or negative FCF
points to reserves, financing, improved operations or dilution. Growth still requires demand, returns on capital,
execution and a sensible price. This score is not converted into any probability of doubling.

Sector adjustments and cash limits
Banks (NU, SOFI, TBBK). Loan origination, deposits and investment cash make industrial FCF/debt ratios
misleading. A separately judged bank rubric uses profitability 25, credit quality 25, funding 20, capital 20 and
allocation 10. Financial dossiers show component points, regulatory capital and the distinction between subsidiary
and parent measures. It is not calibrated to the operating-company scale.

Explicit nonbank adjustments. Earnings-quality points are capped for ONDS, ALM, AMSC, GOOGL, AMZN, FSLR,
NXT and META because reported gains, tax credits or charges complicate quality. Cash points are capped for SYM,
ASML, GEV, MELI, CRWD, ZS, SEDG and ENLT for advances, financial customer funds, compensation or unusual
cash. DE and MELI receive disclosed leverage judgments because consolidated debt includes finance/customer
balances. BLDP liquidity is capped because June cash predates its acquisition. Each dossier lists the actual point
adjustment.

Free cash flow definition. Standardized FCF generally equals operating cash less the capital-expenditure
outflow; NEE also deducts nuclear-fuel spending (USD583m in the latest TTM). It excludes acquisitions, purchased
intangibles not in CapEx and many lease-principal payments; issuer “adjusted FCF” may differ. Positive FCF
generated by working-capital release or advance collections is not necessarily repeatable. Preferred, minority and
tax-equity claims can reduce cash available to common shareholders.

Stock compensation. FCF minus stock-based compensation is shown as a rough economic-charge proxy where
periods match. It is not GAAP, an actual cash payment, a repurchase requirement or a fully diluted valuation.
Options, warrants, convertibles, mergers and ADR ratios need additional analysis beyond a historical share-count
CAGR.

Runway and debt limits. Static runway equals disclosed cash/short investments divided by annualized latest
negative FCF. It excludes future capital raises, additional commitments, restricted-access cash and scheduled
principal payments. It is not a management-guided runway or a solvency forecast. Net debt/EBITDA can be
flattering at a cyclical peak and misleading for banks, finance arms or project structures. The debt-current line
shown is the available reported component, not a complete maturity ladder.

Funds. All nine funds retain N/A for corporate FS and corporate price support. Use portfolio exposures,
concentration, fees, liquidity and structure. For a closed-end fund, NAV premium/discount and the valuation of
private holdings need separate work; assigning a company balance-sheet score to an ETF would be misleading.

Evidence limits. No financial ratio detects every fraud, guarantees recovery of receivables, values every drug
pipeline or proves orders become cash. Source-specific errors and reporting lags remain. The earlier forward
multiples, green flags and scenario probabilities are not statistically validated by this added financial review.

Price-Fundamentals Balance: a price check
This categorical indicator asks whether today’s reported earnings and cash broadly support the stock’s price. It is
a limited valuation screen, with current trailing P/E and P/FCF cross-checked against operating profitability and FS.
It does not claim to calculate equilibrium, intrinsic value or the probability of a future return. Bands are analyst
conventions, not historically optimized thresholds.

Label                       Rule / interpretation

Supported                   Positive operating/net profit and FCF, FS ≥60, and both reported P/E and P/FCF ≤25x. This is at least a 4%
                            reported earnings/cash yield; it does not require growth to be zero or prove value.

Conditional                 Mixed support: growth, cash conversion or financing must justify the multiple. Includes many cases with
                            only one meaningful earnings/cash multiple and no multiple above 40x.

Demanding                   A meaningful P/E or P/FCF exceeds 40x (reported yield below 2.5%). Considerable durable growth may be
                            required; high quality can still earn a demanding price.

Funding-sensitive           An otherwise conditional low-multiple case has FS below 40. Cheap-looking accounting earnings do not
                            repair weak internal funding.

Not established             Current operating profit or meaningful earnings/FCF support is absent. EV/sales provides scale context only.
                            This is common for clinical, research, early-production and distressed companies.


Normalization gates. A nominal Supported result is reduced to Conditional for commodity/memory cyclicals or
material unusual gains, tax-credit reliance, customer advances, stock-compensation/cash-quality issues and
selected investment-heavy cases. Utility/project structures carry explicit residual-equity cautions. These gates
avoid calling a peak-cycle or accounting-driven multiple a reliable bargain.

Bank version. Supported requires FS ≥60, reported P/E ≤20x, P/TBV ≤3x and ROE ≥12%. Otherwise P/E ≤30x is
Conditional; above 30x is Demanding; unavailable earnings are Not established. Credit losses, capital and funding
can still make a low multiple inappropriate. These thresholds do not substitute for a bank residual-income
valuation.

Read growth with the price. Dossiers display historical revenue CAGR, operating and FCF margins, cash
conversion, leverage and dilution alongside the valuation label. Historical growth is not extrapolated into PEG or
fair value. A defensible purchase price would need sector-normalized forecasts, required return, bear/base/bull
value and a margin of safety beyond this screen.

 What qualifies, and what the ranking
 means
 The request is interpreted as ten U.S. companies plus ten non-U.S. companies across solar panels and
 the broader renewable-energy industry. Country grouping follows principal operating headquarters.
 Legal domicile is shown separately: SolarEdge is Israel-headquartered but Delaware-incorporated;
 TOYO has a Japan operating headquarters and Cayman incorporation; Eco Wave Power operates from
 Israel and is Swedish-incorporated.

 This is a bounded, purposive research list, not an exhaustive worldwide optimization. The eligible
 foreign pool is much narrower than the global renewable market. Its bottom ranks should be read as
 watchlist coverage, not ten equally attractive investment recommendations. Strong renewable
 technology alone does not establish sound current-share economics.

 The common factor score weighs profitability/cash and valuation at 20% each; funded growth and
 financial resilience at 15% each; competitive position and repeat demand at 10% each; share allocation
 and execution at 5% each. Each factor receives a judgmental 1-5 grade. Score = sum(grade/5 x
 weight). Ties share ranks, with gaps; rows within ties sort by ticker. The two geographical lists each
 contain ten companies.

  Business exposure                   How to read it

  Direct solar / renewable            Modules, cells, tracking, inverters, project ownership or wave generation are directly
  generation                          connected to the renewable value chain.

  Storage and grid enabling           Batteries, controls and grid equipment help integrate renewables but can also serve
                                      electricity from fossil or nuclear generation. Storage is not itself an energy source.

  Diversified power companies         NEE and GEV have substantial gas, nuclear, utility or other operations. Their
                                      whole-company profits are not pure renewable earnings.

  Hydrogen                            BLDP is included as a conditional renewable-energy enabler. Fuel-cell electricity is
                                      renewable only when the hydrogen supply qualifies as renewable.

  Green shading                       NXT, FSLR and ENLT are qualitative higher-growth research priorities; shading is not
                                      a validated probability, price target or instruction to buy.

  Amber shading                       PBK and BRNX are financially distressed watchlist entries. Inclusion makes the
                                      narrow-universe limitations visible.

 Industry growth, policy and shareholder
 value
 EIA reported planned 2026 U.S. utility-scale additions of 43.4 GW solar, 24 GW battery storage and 11.8
 GW wind. These were developer plans, not completed installations or guaranteed company sales.
 Strong installation growth can coexist with weak manufacturer margins, negative working capital or
 shareholder dilution.

 Capacity plans and their status as projections. EN87

 U.S. tax-credit eligibility and sourcing rules matter materially. IRS instructions state that covered
 wind/solar facilities generally must begin construction by July 4, 2026 or be in service before 2028 to
 qualify for the cited clean electricity production credit, with the specified construction tests and
 exceptions. Separate prohibited-foreign-entity and material-assistance rules affect 45Y, 48E and 45X
 eligibility. This report does not assume every project or component qualifies.

 The production-credit construction rule is not a universal deadline for all storage or manufacturing incentives.
 Company-specific qualification requires its own assessment. EN88, EN89

  Key economic test                    Why it changes the stock case

  Credits and policy-adjusted          Remove the assumption that tax-supported profits are policy-independent. FSLR and
  profit                               NXT both disclose material credit-related economics.

  Backlog quality                      Distinguish binding purchase orders from awarded-but-unsigned work, project
                                       pipelines and framework capacity. Backlog is not cash.

  Per-share funding                    Debt, preferred equity, tax equity, minority interests, warrants and new common
                                       shares decide how much growth reaches today's shareholder.

                                       Generation, EBITDA and operating cash are different measures.

SOLAR + RENEWABLES | OCT 28, 2026 | RESEARCH / CONDITIONAL SCENARIOS                                                E3 / E35

 Three-year estimates: conditional
 illustrations
 The event is a split-adjusted terminal share/ADS price at least twice the reviewed entry quote at the
 last available close on or before October 28, 2029. It is not the chance of briefly touching 2x along the
 way. A double requires 25.99% annual price appreciation. Cash dividends, reinvestment, taxes,
 brokerage/ADR fees and FX drift are excluded; this particularly understates total-return comparison for
 income-oriented utilities.

 The original scenario method is retained. Established companies use 25/50/25, cyclical 30/45/25,
 emerging 35/40/25 and distressed special situations 55/30/15 bear/base/bull weights. Scenario terminal
 medians are analyst judgments. Profitable cases use a forward-to-forward earnings, P/E and net-share
 bridge; turnarounds and development cases use explicit post-financing equity medians. No input is
 selected to force a 60% crossing.

 Each scenario has lognormal dispersion s = 0.50 x max(recent annual volatility, stated floor) x sqrt(3).
 Its 2x tail is weighted into the central illustration. Full-volatility testing changes 0.50 to 1.00. The
 27-case range varies all medians by 0.8/1/1.2, volatility multiplier by 0.35/0.50/0.65, and bear-to-bull
 weights by -10/0/+10 percentage points. Ranges are sensitivities, not confidence intervals. Higher
 volatility can raise or lower an arbitrary threshold probability.

 History comes from split-adjusted daily bars through October 27, 2026. Eighteen companies have
 492-500 returns beginning October 28, 2024. PBK has only 101 returns from June 3, 2026; BRNX only
 51 from August 14. Prior symbols were not spliced into those short series. Illiquidity, corporate actions
 and jumps can distort volatility; no historical average return is extrapolated.

 Historical inputs and adjustment definitions. EN97, EN98

 The half-volatility choice and scenario weights are not empirically calibrated. Lognormal cases omit an
 explicit atom at zero for bankruptcy; qualitative near-zero scenarios cannot capture all failure paths.
 There is no backtested, real-world probability guarantee. A robust internal pass would require the
 central, full-volatility and minimum sensitivity estimates all above 60%; none of these 20 qualifies.

 Market quotes and caps are vendor-reported October 28 intraday views, with separate times on each summary row. They

 Data quality, market caps and buying
 access
 Snapshots use each cited page's reported company market cap and quote. Market cap is not free-float
 value, enterprise value, a guarantee of takeover value or a proxy for safety. The figures are
 approximate vendor estimates and can lag corporate actions. No currency conversion is needed for the
 U.S.-listed quotes; operating results in CAD, EUR and GBP are labeled in company evidence.

 ENLT: do not infer cheapness from inconsistent estimates
 Reported cap USD 8.95B differs by more than 4% from the page quote times its reported shares (USD
 9.36bn). Retained as vendor reported; not used to set the return model.

 Vendor forward P/E changed from 24.51x in the October 27 view to 121.33x in the reviewed October 28
 view; this estimate-basis discrepancy was not reconciled. The return model does not use it.

 The summary retains the latest reviewed cap of USD 8.95B and 121.33x reported forward P/E. Direct equity scenarios
 replace a P/E growth bridge. EN43

 BLDP: acquisition shares and cash changed the picture
 Reported cap USD 550.96M differs by more than 4% from the page quote times its reported shares
 (USD 0.47bn). Retained as vendor reported; not used to set the return model.

 Vendor shares and its +0.46% YoY change predate or omit the roughly 49.6m acquisition shares. The
 reported market cap is retained; pre-deal cash and share fields are not used as a current valuation
 floor.

 The acquired business closed August 28. The Q2 cash balance preceded GBP82.5m of cash consideration and the
 new-share issuance; it is not current cash available for shareholders. EN64, EN66

 Robinhood and the alternative for TURB
 Public Robinhood U.S. pages show affirmative trading language for 19 of the 20 additions. TURB is
 watch-only. Interactive Brokers' public instrument list identifies TURB / Turbo Energy SA; that
 establishes a listed route to investigate, not authenticated permission to open a position. Account type,
 country, trading permissions and current restrictions still need checking.

 IBKR publishes additional permissions and microcap restrictions. Robinhood availability is time-sensitive and may change
 after this review. EN73, EN70, EN71, EN95

 Important exclusions and existing coverage
 Listing and investability were checked before adding companies. Several globally important renewable
 firms fail the requested route, and transaction situations can cap the upside available to today's public
 shareholder. The names below explain those screening decisions; they are not added investment rows.

  Company / situation                    Why it is outside this new top-ten pair

  Daqo New Energy (DQ)                   Issuer identifies NYSE, not Nasdaq. No S&P; 500 eligibility was established;
                                         excluded from the strict listing/index screen.

  Ellomay (ELLO)                         Issuer identifies NYSE American and TASE. NYSE American is not Nasdaq and does
                                         not imply S&P; 500 membership.

  ReNew (RNW)                            Still identifies Nasdaq in its October 27 announcement, but a recommended
                                         USD7.02/share cash acquisition is expected to privatize it. That is a deal-outcome
                                         exposure, not an ordinary three-year public growth case.

  AES (AES)                              A USD15/share cash acquisition has been agreed and shareholders approved it;
                                         expected closing is late 2026 or early 2027. Not selected as an uncapped
                                         long-term growth case.

  NYSE-only or overseas leaders          U.S. ADR access, overseas size or clean-energy-index inclusion alone does not
                                         satisfy Nasdaq-or-S&P-500; eligibility.

  Tesla (TSLA) and Eaton (ETN)           Already covered in the retained report. Tesla has solar/storage alongside autos
                                         and robotics; Eaton is a diversified electrical enabler. They are not counted again.
 Exchange and transaction evidence. EN91, EN90, EN92, EN93, EN94

 What to monitor before updating the view
 Prioritize after-credit cash earnings for FSLR/NXT, cash after interest and project debt for ENLT/NEE, and
 normalized margins without temporary refunds for ENPH/SEDG. For ARRY/CSIQ/FLNC/RUN, require
 improving residual cash per share. For microcaps, funding terms and continued listing can dominate
 technical milestones. Rebuild scenarios when the facts change; do not keep a stale probability.

 NXT is scheduled to report after October 28 close; FSLR on October 29. Those unreleased results are excluded. GEV's
 October 28 morning release is included. Earlier sections retain their original cutoff and assumptions rather than being
 silently refreshed.

 Searching for a 60%+
 three-year doubling case
 25 new stocks across 12 sectors. The updated file contains 89 unique investments: the 64 retained
 investments plus 25 newly assessed companies. The original six themes are covered, together with
 digital banking, e-commerce, cybersecurity, power infrastructure, AI advertising and consumer
 turnarounds.

 Finding: a marginal model pass, no robust qualifier
 Nu Holdings (NU) is the only new stock whose unrounded central model output exceeds 60%. The
 calculator gives 60.6%, but the full-volatility version falls to 53.5% and its sensitivity range is 35%-85%.
 AppLovin (APP) is nearly tied at 59.9%, falling to 53.7% under full volatility. These differences are much
 smaller than the uncertainty in the assumptions.

 Neither company supports a defensible claim of a reliably greater-than-60% real-world likelihood from
 this evidence. No new candidate passes the robustness rule. Nu and AppLovin are the leading
 near-threshold research cases, not certified high-probability investments.

 How the threshold was tested
 The event is a split-adjusted share price at least twice the reviewed entry quote at the last available
 close on or before October 27, 2029. An interim touch of 2x does not qualify. Cash dividends, taxes and
 investor trading/ADR fees are excluded; economic projections hold FX drift constant. A price double
 requires 25.99% compound annual appreciation.

 This is a purposive assessment of 25 additional listed companies, not an exhaustive global screen.
 Candidates were chosen to compare operating growth, valuation, financial capacity and direct or
 enabling exposure across the requested themes. Stocks were retained in the research table even when
 they failed the threshold, so the report does not hide negative findings.

 The prior model settings are retained: established 25/50/25, cyclical 30/45/25, emerging 35/40/25 and
 clinical-binary 45/30/25 bear/base/bull weights. Each terminal-price scenario is lognormal around an
 explicitly stated median. No weights or volatility settings were raised to manufacture a passing stock.

 Central dispersion uses 0.50 x annual sigma x sqrt(3), where sigma is the greater of measured recent
 volatility and an analyst floor. The half-volatility adjustment attempts to limit overlap with business
 scenarios; it was not statistically estimated. The new full-volatility test uses 1.00 x sigma x sqrt(3).
 Neither is a calibrated future-volatility forecast.

 Robust model qualifier is an internal stress rule: the central output, the full-volatility output and the
 lowest of the retained 27 sensitivity cases must all exceed 60%. The 27 cases vary all terminal medians
 by 0.8/1/1.2, dispersion by 0.35/0.50/0.65 and bear/bull weights by 10 percentage points. Passing this
 rule would still not validate a true probability.
 Recent uncertainty inputs are 499 daily log returns per stock, from October 28, 2024 to October 26, 2026. The request
 extended to October 27, but the feed returned observations through October 26; these actual dates are reported.
 Historical means are not extrapolated. Aggregates are split-adjusted, not dividend-adjusted. R89, R90
 Central estimates are rounded to whole percentages to make the threshold audit readable. The calculator decimals shown
 for NU/APP describe arithmetic, not statistical precision. Sensitivity ranges round outward to five points and are not
 confidence intervals.

 What supports a doubling case
  Test                               Evidence sought / reason it matters

  Per-share earnings and cash        Revenue must produce shareholder economics. Distinguish organic growth from
                                     acquired revenue and remove conspicuous nonrecurring gains.

  Entry and exit valuation           A good business can deliver weak returns if the entry multiple is too high. A cheap
                                     multiple can also reflect declining or overstated earnings.

  Funding and dilution               Cash runway, debt service, capex and share issuance decide how much business
                                     upside reaches the current share.

  Repeatable demand and moat         Recurring usage, qualification, customer economics and replacement costs help
                                     assess durability. Orders, program ceilings and demonstrations are not
                                     interchangeable with paid deliveries.

  Downside and concentration         Clinical, policy, credit, commodity, customer and FX shocks can dominate normal
                                     growth. High potential upside is not the same as a high chance of realizing it.

  Historical limits                  The retained 50-year S&P; 500 exercise doubled in 3 of 48 overlapping
                                     three-calendar-year total-return windows. This is context, including dividends, not a
                                     base rate calibrated to these individual price forecasts.
 The historical factor framework in Part B informs these checks. No delisting-inclusive stock model, out-of-sample
 probability calibration or new 50-year stock-by-stock backtest was performed. Long-horizon parameter uncertainty remains
 material. R88, R91

 Important interpretation details
 For profitable companies the base bridge is aggregate normalized earnings growth, an exit forward P/E
 and a separate net share-count assumption. Direct equity-value scenarios are used for clinical
 platforms, loss-making or transformed businesses and the valuation-constrained CrowdStrike case.
 Those scenarios include funding and dilution judgments; they are not full discounted-cash-flow or
 risk-adjusted pipeline valuations.

 Forward P/E comes from the reviewed vendor snapshot and may use a different estimate basis or
 update time from management guidance. SoFi and The Bancorp show material guidance/vendor gaps;
 the lower vendor-implied starting earnings are retained rather than treating the difference as certain
 upside. Bank EV, debt/FCF and generic industrial ROIC are not used as valuation proof.
 Quote and market-cap rows are in USD, mostly at October 27 close. TBBK is the reviewed 2:07 p.m. intraday quote. Issuer
 currencies are named where relevant. Snapshots are not synchronized or independently reconstructed. Public Robinhood
 U.S. pages support access labels; personal-account and country eligibility were not authenticated. R92

 Why one percentage point is not an edge
 The threshold audit is almost a tie: NU calculates to 60.6% and APP to 59.9%. Both round to roughly
 60% at the original report's five-point precision. It would be misleading to treat the 0.7-point difference
 as an empirically meaningful distinction or to promote either stock into a high-confidence basket.

  Nu scenario change                                                                                 Central illustration

  Locked central assumptions                                                                         60.6%

  Aggregate earnings growth 20%/yr; other inputs unchanged                                           49.6%

  Aggregate earnings growth 25%/yr; other inputs unchanged                                           55.5%

  Aggregate earnings growth 35%/yr; other inputs unchanged                                           64.7%

  No base-case P/E rerating from the entry multiple                                                  53.0%

  All terminal values 20% lower                                                                      48.7%

  Full historical volatility, instead of half                                                        53.5%

 The current investment case for Nu is profitable customer growth at a relatively low earnings multiple.
 The competing explanation is that consumer credit, currency and country risks deserve that discount.
 For AppLovin, high cash profits and a moderate forward P/E are attractive, while advertising-platform
 and privacy changes can be discontinuous risks. These alternatives belong in the analysis rather than
 being hidden inside a precise-looking percentage.
 NU issuer operating and credit evidence; APP issuer financial evidence. R46, R47, R76
 The altered growth rates, P/E and terminal values are sensitivity examples, not new forecasts. A 20% terminal-value
 haircut is not an exchange-rate prediction. None of these tests estimates every possible failure mode.

 on spending.

 valuation-basis risk.

 damage demand.

 new cohort.

 Research priorities and monitoring
 NU and APP are the clearest near-threshold cases in this new cohort; both require further underwriting
 of business risks rather than a claim that their true odds exceed 60%. VRT offers a tangible
 cash-generating AI infrastructure business; SOFI has stronger near-term growth but more credit,
 funding and dilution sensitivity. CACI, BWXT and ETN supply durable franchises with lower modeled
 doubling probabilities at the reviewed prices.

 For the original themes, the new screen does not replace earlier research priorities simply because a
 speculative name has a large bull-case target. RCAT/ONDS rely on production, profitable integration
 and per-share funding discipline. ADPT/ABCL require reimbursement, separation terms or clinical
 evidence. Those milestones are different from an established earnings compounder.

 Success factors from five decades of
 markets
 The requested 50-year perspective is 1976-2026. This update synthesizes published studies whose
 samples overlap much of that period and, in some cases, extend earlier. It does not run a new 50-year
 backtest of these investments; many did not exist for that long. Success means durable shareholder
 value and returns after the price paid, not revenue growth alone.

 independently proven return premiums. Factors overlap, so the score is not a sum of independent effects.

 How the factor scores and ranks work
 Each company receives eight evidence-based grades, from 1 (weak or unproven) to 5 (exceptionally
 strong). A 1 can reflect an early business or insufficient commercial evidence, rather than proof that
 the company cannot succeed. The rubric favors demonstrated economics and can rank early biotech
 or robotics ventures below their possible upside.

   Code      5 | strongest evidence                3 | mixed evidence                    1 | weak / unproven


   P         strong recurring economics and        profitable but cyclical or            operating profits/cash generation
             cash evidence                         cash-conversion gaps                  absent or unproven.


   V         compelling established earnings       reasonable but demanding or           extreme price assumptions or no
             anchor                                cycle-dependent                       reliable pro forma anchor.


   G         demonstrated commercial               credible but cyclical or              largely unfunded or unvalidated
             growth with financing capacity        ramp-dependent                        future growth.


   S         strong funding buffer                 manageable debt or finite             major unresolved financing or
                                                   runway                                transaction risk.


   M         unusually strong established          useful differentiation with           durable advantage not
             barriers                              competition                           demonstrated.


   D         strong repeat-use or service          cyclical or limited recurring         demand is mainly pre-commercial.
             evidence                              revenue


   A         unusually strong demonstrated         mixed or limited reviewed             severe dilution or unproven
             per-share discipline                  evidence                              ownership economics.


   X         broad demand and consistent           material but manageable               severe concentration, binary or
             execution                             operating exposures                   transaction dependence.


 Transparent arithmetic and tie rules
 Score = sum of (factor grade / 5) x factor weight, giving 20-100 points. Example: Intuitive Surgical
 scores 20 + 12 + 15 + 15 + 10 + 10 + 4 + 4 = 90. Scores are rounded to whole points and are not
 expected returns, success probabilities, target prices or statistical forecasts.

 Within each row, factors rank by grade, with ties ordered by framework priority. All eight company
 factors, or all six fund factors, are shown in the companion table. Overall ranks now compare 55
 companies separately from nine funds. Adding eight names changes peer rank, while earlier factor
 grades are retained. Equal scores share rank; subsequent numbers skip. Differences below five points
 are broadly similar, not precise superiority.
 Higher / medium / lower evidence labels describe disclosure and interpretation limits in the reviewed material, not
 confidence in future returns. No uniform ten-year ROIC series, accrual model, beta, live liquidity test or independent
 forensic audit was computed. A one-grade change to a 20%-weight factor moves the total four points.
 Green HIGH marks the earlier growth selection, a different judgment from factor alignment. It does not mean the highest
 factor score. Original theme ranks are retained; the added factor rank answers a separate question. Tail risks, including
 Taiwan disruption, clinical failure or transaction failure, can overwhelm a strong composite.

                                        Evaluate investment returns and per-share economics, not expansion spending

   Bessembinder, US through             A small minority of stocks explains net wealth creation: about 4% in the US study
   2016; global 1990-2020               and 2.4% globally. Diversification matters; inspecting famous surviving winners
                                        alone creates selection bias. S93, S94


   Bessembinder, US return              Long holding periods contribute materially to extreme cumulative outcomes. A
   histories 1925-2023                  historical winner table describes outcomes; it does not identify tomorrow's
                                        winners. S95

 Samples, methods and definitions differ; the research does not establish one universal ranking of success factors across all
 sectors or all five decades. This is a qualitative application to the report's October 27, 2026 evidence and valuation
 snapshots, not a claim of causal proof or out-of-sample validation.

 The nine funds use a separate rubric
 An ETF or closed-end fund has fees, a portfolio, governance and trading mechanics. Treating its
 expense ratio as corporate valuation, or assigning it the earnings of a single constituent, would distort
 the comparison. These fund grades assess structure and disclosed exposure; no weighted
 holdings-level factor portfolio was calculated.

   Priority / weight                       Fund factor and test


   1. C | 25%                              Recurring fund expense; net waivers and CEF estimates are explicitly
   Cost discipline                         identified.


   2. B | 20%                              Issuer and country breadth plus concentration; all nine remain narrow themes.
   Diversification


   3. T | 20%                              Published holdings, observable underlying prices and NAV reliability; actual
   Disclosure and price discovery          bid-ask spreads are not measured.


   4. E | 15%                              How directly the disclosed mandate serves the stated theme, not whether the
   Economic exposure fit                   theme will outperform.


   5. Q | 10%                              Qualitative maturity of targeted businesses. No weighted portfolio profitability
   Commercial maturity                     or valuation is claimed.


   6. R | 10%                              Transparent index rules or active-manager constraints, governance and
   Mandate discipline                      strategy changes.


 Scoring anchors and scope
 Cost C: 5 at 0.20% or less; 4 above 0.20%-0.40%; 3 above 0.40%-0.65%; 2 above 0.65%-1.00%; 1
 above 1.00%. These cutoffs are analyst choices. Net waivers can expire and BOT costs are estimates.
 A cheap fund can still own expensive or risky assets.

 Thematic baskets are capped at 3/5 on breadth B because they retain sector risk; concentrated listed
 baskets can score 2 and private portfolios 1. T evaluates disclosure and price discovery, not a
 measured bid-ask spread. E grades fit to each fund's own stated theme. Q grades commercial
 maturity qualitatively. R grades mandate discipline; recent name/index changes and active discretion
 warrant review.
 SEC guidance explains the compounding drag of recurring fees. SPIVA persistence research cautions against selecting
 funds simply because of recent winners. Neither source validates this particular score or predicts which of these nine funds
 will outperform. S96, S97
 The leading funds in this rubric are still concentrated sector tools, not broad-market core portfolios. Company and fund
 scores use different definitions and are ranked separately.

 Three-year doubling: what is estimated
 The event is a split-adjusted share price at least 2.00 times the entry price at the last available close
 on or before October 27, 2029. The entry is the price represented by the cited October 27, 2026
 valuation snapshot; those quotes and financial estimates are not synchronized. These are conditional
 research estimates, not executable entry prices or promised price targets.

 Doubling requires 25.99% compound annual price growth. A business growing earnings at 20% a year
 reaches only 1.73x in three years if its P/E and share count are unchanged. If the P/E falls 20%, the
 result is about 1.38x. Revenue growth, business quality, the green HIGH flag and a probability of
 doubling are therefore separate measures.

   Included in the model             Definition / limitation


   Terminal price, not an interim    A stock that touches 2x and later falls below it does not satisfy this event.
   peak                              First-touch probabilities would be higher and are not calculated.


   Price appreciation                Cash dividends, dividend reinvestment, taxes and investor trading/ADR charges are
                                     excluded. Fund operating costs are reflected in fund scenarios. A total-return
                                     investment can do better than its price-only result.


   Foreign listings and share        Company economics are assessed with FX held constant. USD ADR history is
   classes                           identified when used to inform uncertainty for a foreign home listing. Actual USD
                                     and local-currency doubling outcomes can differ. GOOGL/GOOG remain one
                                     company.


   Subjective scenario model         No dataset here establishes the true probability for any one security. Outputs
                                     depend on analyst assumptions about bear/base/bull outcomes and weights. All
                                     model-evidence labels are low or very low.


   No portfolio probability          The 64 outcomes are correlated. These percentages must not be added, averaged
                                     into a portfolio success rate, or treated as independent bets.

 Return-definition and projection limits are consistent with the SEC performance-claims guidance. S116

 Historical evidence and its limits
 Using NYU/Damodaran annual S&P 500 total returns for 1976-2025, 3 of 48 overlapping
 three-calendar-year windows doubled: 6.25%. They were 1995-1997, 1996-1998 and 1997-1999. This
 is a broad-index historical frequency including dividends, not an individual-stock price-only probability
 and not a calibration of this model.
 Calculation: multiply (1 + annual return) for each consecutive three-year window and count products >= 2.00. The 48
 windows share observations and are not 48 independent experiments. The source table was updated January 5, 2026; the
 calculation uses the 50 complete years through 2025. S110, S114

 For individual uncertainty, the connected price feed supplied approximately two recent years of
 split-adjusted daily closing prices, generally October 28, 2024-October 26, 2026. Older history was
 outside the connected plan. Annual realized volatility is sample standard deviation of daily log returns
 times the square root of 252. Historical return means are not extrapolated into the forecast.
 Recent price data: Massive aggregate bars, adjusted=true. Bars are split-adjusted and exclude dividend adjustment. No
 stock-level three-year historical doubling frequency is claimed because the available own-security histories do not span
 that horizon. NYU is a separate source for the long-run benchmark. S111, S112

 Short-listed histories, business transformations and mandate changes require explicit proxies. SK
 hynix uses Micron volatility because its U.S. ADR is new; Insilico uses XBI; FFR and BOT use BOTZ;
 KOID/BOTT use BOTZ; EART uses REMX because its mandate changed. Proxies inform dispersion only.
 They do not become the company's own performance record or imply equivalent holdings.

 USAR excludes its earlier cash-shell period; Generate excludes pre-IPO dates. Foreign OTC/ADR series
 may be less liquid and embed FX. Minimum volatility assumptions prevent a quiet or stale recent
 sample from implying unrealistic certainty. Every scenario record states the input ticker, dates,
 observations, measured volatility and floor.
 Listing-history checks: USAR began trading March 14, 2025; GENB began February 27, 2026. S118, S117
 Long-horizon uncertainty can remain large even with extensive history. The historical success-factor research elsewhere in
 the report informs growth moderation, cash discipline, valuation and dilution checks; it does not validate these
 probabilities. S113, S91, S93

 The probability model: fully specified
 Each investment has three terminal price medians, expressed as multiples of its entry price: bear,
 base and bull. Each scenario has a lognormal distribution around its median. The scenario weights
 below are policy judgments based on business maturity and cyclicality, not empirically estimated
 frequencies. The base median is not the mean or median of the combined distribution.

   Scenario class               Bear / base / bull weights    Application


   Established                  25% / 50% / 25%               Profitable, established franchises


   Cyclical                     30% / 45% / 25%               Industrial, equipment, commodity or program-cycle
                                                              exposure


   Emerging                     35% / 40% / 25%               Scaling, expensive or not yet sustainably
                                                              cash-generative


   Clinical binary              45% / 30% / 25%               Clinical platform outcomes and financing dominate


   Transaction special          55% / 30% / 15%               FFR: pending restructuring and extreme dilution
   situation


   Thematic ETF                 25% / 50% / 25%               Listed equity baskets; still concentrated by sector


   Private-asset CEF            40% / 35% / 25%               BOT: private marks, costs and NAV premium uncertainty


 Arithmetic
 Let m be a scenario's terminal price median and w its weight. Annual sigma is the larger of measured
 recent volatility and the row's analyst floor. Set s = 0.50 x sigma x sqrt(3). Then probability of
 doubling = sum of w x [1 - Phi((ln(2) - ln(m)) / s)]. Phi is the standard-normal cumulative distribution.
 Severe-loss probability uses the same distributions below 0.50x.

 The one-half volatility multiplier is an analyst overlap adjustment: scenario medians already include
 business and valuation uncertainty, so adding full realized volatility could count part of that
 uncertainty twice. This adjustment is not statistically estimated. Its sensitivity is tested; it is not a
 claim that future volatility will halve.
 The deterministic formula uses no random simulation seed. Central percentages round to the nearest 5 points. Values
 below 5% or above 95% use <5% or >95%; they never assert impossible or certain outcomes. Full unrounded results are
 retained in the calculation record.

 Assumptions, sensitivity and interpretation
 For profitable companies, base-case checks connect aggregate normalized earnings growth, an exit
 P/E and net share-count change. Approximate price multiple = (1 + earnings growth)^3 x (exit P/E /
 entry P/E) / (1 + net dilution)^3. Forward earnings are compared with an equivalent forward basis at
 the horizon. Rounded scenario medians express a wider operating judgment rather than precise price
 targets.

 For cash-burning businesses, project developers and clinical platforms, direct post-financing
 equity-value scenarios are used. They account qualitatively for cash, debt, capex, milestones and
 dilution. They are not a complete discounted cash-flow or asset-by-asset risk-adjusted NAV model.
 EV/sales or EV/EBITDA is never mechanically substituted for share-price appreciation. Contingent
 licensing headlines are not booked as assured revenue.

 For ETFs, scenarios are basket price outcomes after the stated operating-cost assumptions. No
 holdings-level earnings forecast or portfolio simulation was fitted. For BOT, a synchronized
 market-price/NAV premium was not verified; its estimate is especially fragile and uses wide
 assumptions. Future fee-waiver expiry is allowed for KOID and THNQ.

 What the range means
 Each range spans 27 combinations: terminal medians multiplied by 0.80, 1.00 or 1.20; residual
 volatility multiplier 0.35, 0.50 or 0.65; and a 10-percentage-point shift toward bear or bull, or
 unchanged weights. Base weight stays fixed. Bounds round outward to five points. This is a sensitivity
 envelope under chosen assumptions, not a 90% or 95% confidence interval, and not every plausible
 outcome lies inside it.

 No out-of-sample calibration, option-implied forecast, delisting-inclusive stock base-rate model or full
 fifty-year backtest of these 64 investments was performed. Parameter uncertainty, regime shifts,
 market closures, total loss, FX shocks and changing business models can defeat the model. Small
 differences between estimates are not investment superiority.
 Clinical context: BIO/Informa/QLS found 7.9% overall approval likelihood from Phase I across 2011-2020, varying by
 indication and modality. That is neither a three-year endpoint nor a stock-return probability. It motivates substantial failure
 scenarios, not a mechanical 7.9% assignment to any named company. S115
 Higher speculative upside can accompany higher severe-loss risk. Read the operating requirements and downside beside
 the percentage; retain the earlier factor scores as a separate quality and price discipline check.

 How to read the rankings
 The original global shortlist comprises 42 companies, seven per theme. This edition includes 13
 additional companies and nine funds, giving 64 investments in total. The eight newest additions are
 U.S.-headquartered listed companies with direct or enabling physical-AI exposure. Selection weighs
 commercial relevance, financial capacity and complementary roles; it is not an exhaustive global
 screen or a claim of maximum future returns.

   Major factor                What matters for the investment


   Actual exposure             Revenue from robots, chips, materials or drug discovery; direct products versus enabling
                               components or a small optional business.


   Competitive position        Qualification barriers, installed base, intellectual property, proprietary data, manufacturing
                               yields and switching costs.


   Growth and catalysts        Order conversion, product adoption, capacity ramp, trials and partner payments, with
                               dates checked for later revisions.


   Financial resilience        Operating cash flow, capital spending, debt, cash runway, stock compensation, ownership
                               claims and dilution.


   Valuation                   Forward P/E for established earners; normalized cycle economics for commodities;
                               EV/sales or risk-adjusted pipeline value for loss-makers.


   Downside and thesis         A concrete operational, commercial or financing development that would require
   failure                     reconsideration.


 Interpretation and data conventions
 Risk labels are relative assessments, not probabilities or maximum loss estimates. "Consider
 selectively" identifies a credible candidate at the displayed valuation; "watch price" calls for a better
 entry or stronger evidence; "cyclical opportunity" requires normalized earnings analysis; "speculative"
 entails substantial financing, execution or binary clinical risk.

 Company financial figures refer to the stated fiscal period, which differs across issuers. Market
 multiples are rounded snapshots retrieved October 27, 2026 from Stock Analysis. Pages mix real-time
 and delayed market data and are not synchronized executable quotes. Forecast P/E may use adjusted
 earnings and varying estimate windows; it is not directly comparable to audited GAAP P/E or to a
 multiple calculated from management guidance.
 Market capitalizations were refreshed separately from Stock Analysis on October 27, 2026. They are rounded vendor
 equity values, not enterprise values, free floats, AUM or fully diluted transaction values. USD is used for U.S.-listed
 issuer/ADR pages; other listings retain their stated currency, with no FX conversion. ADR and ordinary listings are not
 added together. Share classes, share-count revisions and pending deals can affect the basis. This cap-only refresh does not
 update earnings, valuation grades or the original research cutoff.
 The connected Massive subscription did not include valuation ratios. Public company disclosures and Stock Analysis were
 used instead. Public vendor ratios are not independently audited or fully reconstructed here; check the linked underlying
 filing and live quote before acting.
 FCF = free cash flow. EV = enterprise value. EBITDA = earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization. TTM =
 trailing twelve months. N/M = not meaningful. A low P/E during a commodity earnings peak can be a warning rather than a
 bargain.

 How to interpret the labels
 RH U.S.: Yes means the asset-specific public page promotes trading that ticker. ADR routes represent
 the same underlying company, but are different securities from the home-exchange shares. Dollar
 quotes, ADR ratios, depositary fees, spreads and liquidity can differ. SKHY began Nasdaq trading in
 July 2026; ten SKHY ADRs represent one Korean ordinary share.
 SK hynix listing and receipt basis. S108, S109
 Neo's asset-specific page uses watch-only wording, so it is treated as unavailable for a new purchase despite a generic
 Buy/sign-up section. A quote page alone is not proof of purchase support. S104
 IBKR = Interactive Brokers. The named alternatives are documented exchange-access routes; individual security and
 account order eligibility were not authenticated. Enable the relevant country's stock permissions and confirm the exact
 company/exchange in the order ticket. Residence, IBKR entity, FX funding, trading lots, fees, halts and temporary
 restrictions can affect access. Final availability is the buy/order eligibility shown in your account. S105, S106, S107

 What the themes share
 Physical AI combines sensing, computing and action. A company can be commercially important to
 robotics while deriving only a small share of sales from robots. This report separates direct platforms
 from enabling sensors, controls and software. Remotely operated systems and surgeon-controlled
 robots are not described as fully autonomous.

 Rare materials are interpreted broadly as rare earths, critical minerals and engineered specialty
 materials. Lithium, titanium and nickel are not rare-earth elements. Commodity abundance,
 processing difficulty, supply concentration and customer qualification are different issues; owning a
 deposit alone does not establish a profitable business.
 Materials definitions and uses are grounded in the USGS 2026 Mineral Commodity Summaries and issuer product
 disclosures. S74

 Defense spending is a multi-year demand driver. NATO allies committed to a 2035 target combining at
 least 3.5% of GDP for core defense with up to 1.5% for broader defense and security investment. It is
 not an immediate 5%-of-GDP equipment order, and national appropriations and execution still matter.
 NATO source, updated June 29, 2026. S73


 Accounting checks that change the conclusion

   Company / issue               Research implication


   Tempus: investment            Q2 GAAP net income was $5.6m, including $98.5m unrealized investment gains. Do not
   gains                         assume underlying operating profitability from the headline. S39


   Schrodinger:                  A gain associated with the Ajax transaction contributed to Q2 net income. Contract

 3. Rare and critical materials
 This category covers rare earths and other strategically important materials. Lithium, titanium and
 nickel are not rare-earth elements. Several selections are processors or qualified materials
 manufacturers rather than miners; commercial value often lies in processing and customer
 qualification.

 What each material does

   Company                   Material functionality


   Lynas                     NdPr: compact permanent magnets. Dy/Tb: improved high-temperature magnet
                             performance in motors and aerospace.


   Albemarle                 Lithium: rechargeable batteries for vehicles, mobile robots and storage. Bromine: industrial
                             specialties.


   Neo                       Rare-earth magnetics: motors. Hafnium: advanced electronics and high-temperature
                             materials.


   Materion                  Stiff, light beryllium: aerospace optics and structures. Beryllium alloys: demanding
                             electrical components.


   ATI                       Titanium: lightweight, corrosion-resistant structures. Nickel superalloys: hot turbine
                             components.


   MP Materials              NdPr: permanent magnets for compact motors and robotics; heavy rare earths broaden
                             performance.


   Almonty                   Tungsten: hard cutting tools and dense, heat-resistant industrial, aerospace and defense
                             components.

 Material functions: USGS mineral summaries and issuer product disclosures. S23, S28


 Where the economic value sits
 Lynas and MP combine resources with separation and downstream expansion. Neo provides
 processing and magnetic materials. Materion and ATI earn value through specialized manufacturing
 and customer qualification. Albemarle is a lithium-cycle exposure, while Almonty depends heavily on a
 tungsten production ramp. These are different business models, so a single commodity multiple is not
 an adequate comparison.

 The four most compelling combinations of existing economics and displayed valuation are TSMC,
 NVIDIA, General Dynamics and Regeneron. The next three research priorities for broader theme
 coverage are FANUC, Teledyne and Lynas. This is an ordered diligence queue, not an equal-weight
 recommendation.

   Research priority                 What to verify before committing capital


   TSMC / NVIDIA                     Test the earnings case under slower AI spending and lower margins; accept that both
                                     carry substantial common customer-cycle exposure.


   General Dynamics /                Verify normalized free cash flow and the durability of the existing franchise; compare
   Regeneron                         the price with conservative earnings assumptions.


   FANUC / Teledyne                  Check order durability, organic growth and returns on capital; require that the
                                     premium remains supported by cash generation.


   Lynas / Albemarle / Neo           Use normalized material prices, include expansion spending, and distinguish saleable
                                     product from nameplate capacity.


   AI-native biotech / direct        Size around financing and failure risk; require clinical evidence or funded production
   autonomy                          rather than relying on partnership ceilings and demonstrations.


 How the additions affect the original selections
 ABB is divesting Robotics to SoftBank; it is therefore a changing exposure rather than a stable
 long-term robotics proxy. The latest reviewed quarterly filing expected completion in Q4 2026.
 SoftBank itself introduces a much broader set of investment and financing exposures.
 ABB transaction sources. S75, S76

 AMD and Arm remain relevant businesses, but displayed forward P/Es of about 49x and 94x
 respectively set a higher hurdle than the selected large chip franchises. Tesla is now included in the
 requested additions. Its updated 189.9x forward earnings snapshot still requires substantial future
 success; it has not been moved into the original physical-AI top seven.
 Peer valuation snapshots, retrieved October 27, 2026. S77, S78, S79

 Red Cat offers more direct small-drone exposure, but was not preferred over the selected established
 platforms and component suppliers. Its negative earnings, limited operating history at scale and
 financing risk call for a different risk budget.
 Red Cat snapshot. S80

 Valuation and concentration stress tests
 A great business can produce a weak stock return if earnings disappoint or the valuation contracts.
 The simple illustration below assumes 10% annual EPS growth for five years and a 25x terminal P/E. It
 excludes dividends, tax, fees, dilution and changes in net cash. It is a mathematical sensitivity, not a
 forecast for any company.

   Entry P/E                                 Annualized price return                   Five-year price return


   20x                                       15.0%                                     101.3%


   30x                                       6.1%                                      34.2%


   40x                                       0.1%                                      0.7%


   50x                                       -4.2%                                     -19.5%

 Calculation: annualized return = (1 + EPS growth) x (exit P/E / entry P/E)^(1/5) - 1. The same growth rate gives very
 different outcomes at different entry prices.
